html:
Tech-enablement theses by portfolio company

Each portfolio company gets a named operating system built mostly from proven vendors plus a thin BSP data layer. The goal is to make earnings look more predictable, recurring and scalable to the next buyer, or, at Thomas Scientific, to lift EBITDA directly (ServiceOS evidence, Oct 6, 2026).

Common logic

  • Bankers price quality. PKF puts project-heavy, low-retention HVAC firms at 5-6x EBITDA and repeatable-service firms at 10x+. Capstone/IMAP show 6.8x typical versus 9.8x premium (ServiceOS evidence).
  • Up to ~3 turns of premium is supported. Tech enablement can claim about 0.5-2.5 turns of it. The 17-20x roll-up prints reflect scale, not technology (ServiceOS evidence).
  • 45 agents across the six companies are worth est. $12.7M a year of run-rate EBITDA-equivalent once ramped. These figures rest on analyst assumptions and are not de-duplicated (Portfolio AI-agent plan).

Company theses

Punctual ProsServiceOS (ServiceTitan)Raise call booking (38% average vs 59% at 25+ tech shops), pricebook tickets and membership density1.0-2.5$0.9M

Sources: ServiceOS evidence; Portfolio AI-agent plan.

Evidence strength

  • Punctual Pros: strong for direction, medium for size. Public residential comps suggest a mid-teens EBITDA margin is the realistic mature target (Public comparables).
  • CET and Frontline: medium. Electrical M&A slowed to 99 deals in 2025. Frontline's entry multiple is already est. ~12-15x (ServiceOS evidence).
  • Thomas Scientific: weak for multiple, medium for EBITDA. Leverage and capital structure drive this exit, not rerating (ServiceOS evidence).
  • BPI: medium. The case rests on the PPHC ~8.4x floor versus an est. 10-13x sponsor exit (ServiceOS evidence).
  • Fair Harbor: the premium range and full thesis are truncated in the context. The full HarborOS section of ServiceOS evidence would answer this.

Caveats

  • Champions (~18.5x) and Sila (~17x) are press estimates (ServiceOS evidence).
  • Agent volumes are analyst estimates. Most metric claims come from vendor case studies (Portfolio AI-agent plan).

Next actions

  • Replace the assumed call, ticket, invoice and member volumes with system-of-record counts at each portfolio company.
  • Pull the full SignalOS and HarborOS sections to complete the BPI and Fair Harbor theses and the Fair Harbor turn range.
  • Set wave 1 baselines for the inbound-contact and document agents before launch.
  • Re-test Thomas Scientific value against EBITDA and leverage targets rather than multiple expansion.

# Tech-enablement theses by portfolio company

Each portfolio company gets a named operating system built mostly from proven vendors plus a thin BSP data layer. The goal is to make earnings look more predictable, recurring and scalable to the next buyer, or, at Thomas Scientific, to lift EBITDA directly (ServiceOS evidence, Oct 6, 2026).

## Common logic

- Bankers price quality. PKF puts project-heavy, low-retention HVAC firms at 5-6x EBITDA and repeatable-service firms at 10x+. Capstone/IMAP show 6.8x typical versus 9.8x premium (ServiceOS evidence).
- Up to ~3 turns of premium is supported. Tech enablement can claim about 0.5-2.5 turns of it. The 17-20x roll-up prints reflect scale, not technology (ServiceOS evidence).
- 45 agents across the six companies are worth est. $12.7M a year of run-rate EBITDA-equivalent once ramped. These figures rest on analyst assumptions and are not de-duplicated (Portfolio AI-agent plan).

## Company theses

| Company | OS and core stack | Thesis | Tech premium (est. turns) | Agent value (est.) |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| Punctual Pros | ServiceOS (ServiceTitan) | Raise call booking (38% average vs 59% at 25+ tech shops), pricebook tickets and membership density | 1.0-2.5 | $0.9M |
| CET | GridOS (Procore) | Turn project work into recurring solar/SCADA O&M; NuWave and EV monitoring; better bid selection | 0.5-1.5 | $1.3M |
| Frontline | FirmOS (ConnectWise/Kaseya) | Grow security and e-billing revenue-cycle lines; reduce churn | 0.5-1.5 | $3.6M |
| Thomas Scientific | LabOS (Shopify Plus/Coupa) | Cut cost-to-serve and shift transactions to digital; Avantor ~80% digital as benchmark | 0.5-1.0 | $3.8M |
| BPI | SignalOS (Brandwatch/Zignal) | Productize monitoring; draft faster while protecting client confidentiality | 0.5-2.0 | $2.3M |
| Fair Harbor | HarborOS (Shopify/Klaviyo) | Cut returns and excess inventory | Not in shown data | $0.8M |

Sources: ServiceOS evidence; Portfolio AI-agent plan.

## Evidence strength

- **Punctual Pros:** strong for direction, medium for size. Public residential comps suggest a mid-teens EBITDA margin is the realistic mature target (Public comparables).
- **CET and Frontline:** medium. Electrical M&A slowed to 99 deals in 2025. Frontline's entry multiple is already est. ~12-15x (ServiceOS evidence).
- **Thomas Scientific:** weak for multiple, medium for EBITDA. Leverage and capital structure drive this exit, not rerating (ServiceOS evidence).
- **BPI:** medium. The case rests on the PPHC ~8.4x floor versus an est. 10-13x sponsor exit (ServiceOS evidence).
- **Fair Harbor:** the premium range and full thesis are truncated in the context. The full HarborOS section of ServiceOS evidence would answer this.

## Caveats

- Champions (~18.5x) and Sila (~17x) are press estimates (ServiceOS evidence).
- Agent volumes are analyst estimates. Most metric claims come from vendor case studies (Portfolio AI-agent plan).

## Next actions

- Replace the assumed call, ticket, invoice and member volumes with system-of-record counts at each portfolio company.
- Pull the full SignalOS and HarborOS sections to complete the BPI and Fair Harbor theses and the Fair Harbor turn range.
- Set wave 1 baselines for the inbound-contact and document agents before launch.
- Re-test Thomas Scientific value against EBITDA and leverage targets rather than multiple expansion.
